question: What is the smallest cross-anchor sewing that reduces the two typed local-intertwiner scalars to one while preserving J, grading, Pati-Salam covariance and the absence of physical mixed I-N support?

boundedModel.relationSheetAssignment: the primitive D sector and primitive M sector of claim 1127 occupy opposite Gamma_rel sheets; J supplies their conjugate partner sectors
boundedModel.patiSalamAssumption: a candidate sewing is a Pati-Salam scalar on relation multiplicity; if its two endpoint gauge irreps are inequivalent, Schur's lemma sets it to zero

ordinaryCarrierSewing.candidate: a linear map S:V_D->V_M adjoined with its reverse as an off-diagonal carrier operator T_S

classification.verdict: equates scalars but generates all of M_4(C)
equates scalars but generates all of M_4(C)

ordinaryCarrierSewing.generalTheorem: Because the linear span of M_2 S M_2 equals M_2 for every nonzero 2x2 matrix S, one nonzero carrier sewing plus the two full local matrix algebras generates both cross blocks and hence M_4(C).
ordinaryCarrierSewing.relationParity: Every direct D-to-M carrier block is Gamma_rel-odd in the actual primitive-sector assignment. Its J-completed partner is also odd. Therefore a nonzero direct sewing cannot belong to the Gamma_rel-even allowed operator algebra.
ordinaryCarrierSewing.koGrading: Homogeneous chirality-even and chirality-odd nonzero S both exist, so KO grading alone does not select a safe nonzero carrier sewing.
ordinaryCarrierSewing.patiSalamCovariance: When the relation sectors carry equivalent Pati-Salam representations, S tensor I_gauge is covariant and the M_4 closure no-go remains. When they are inequivalent, the scalar Hom vanishes and no sewing occurs.

canonicalJunkQualification.model: Ignore the actual relation-sheet parity and restrict a carrier sewing to the two P-lifts, producing the four-vertex chain I_D-P_D-P_M-N_M with diagonal algebra C^4.
canonicalJunkQualification.inducedMixedSupport: The I_D-N_M endpoint matrix is a length-three composite and is algebraically composable.
canonicalJunkQualification.degreeThreeCalculation: The represented degree-three space has dimension 8 and is entirely junk, so Omega_D^3=0 and the length-three endpoint vanishes in this canonical toy quotient.
canonicalJunkQualification.boundary: This junk rescue does not make the physical sewing viable: the primitive P_D-P_M edge is Gamma_rel-odd on the actual KO-6 labels, and the matrix-valued physical junk quotient has not been computed for a regraded or stabilized carrier.

coefficientLineSewing.construction: Introduce one common coefficient line L and nonzero embeddings i_D:L->L_D and i_M:L->L_M. Equivalently impose y=kappa d with fixed nonzero kappa, without adding a morphism V_D->V_M.
coefficientLineSewing.packetConsequence: Every mediator copy has (d_i,y_i)=lambda_i(1,kappa), so all columns lie on one projective Schur ray.
coefficientLineSewing.jCompatibility: On the J-conjugate sheet use the conjugate embeddings; kappa_- equals conjugate(kappa_+).
coefficientLineSewing.gradingCompatibility: The equalizer is degree zero and relation-sheet even because it relates coefficient functors rather than carrier states.
coefficientLineSewing.patiSalamCovariance: L, L_D and L_M are scalar coefficient lines multiplying already-fixed Pati-Salam Clebsch intertwiners.
coefficientLineSewing.mixedSupport: No cross-sector one-arrow is added, so X_D X_M remains zero and I-N remains noncomposable; all previously computed junk spaces are unchanged.
coefficientLineSewing.classification: Every nonzero sewing of two one-dimensional coefficient lines is isomorphic to this construction. With fixed metrics kappa retains a normalized phase; J pairs it with its complex conjugate.
coefficientLineSewing.status: formally viable and minimal, but it is a single-common-source or single-spurion axiom, not derived from the current Spin(2,3), Jordan or Pati-Salam carrier

minimalityTheorem.statement: There is no nonzero ordinary carrier-linear sewing in the bounded two-sector model that both reduces the commutant to one and preserves noncomposability. One nonzero coefficient-line equalizer is the smallest non-carrier enlargement that does both.
minimalityTheorem.whyMinimal: The unsewn compatible coefficient endomorphisms form C^2. Reducing them to the diagonal C requires one independent nonzero compatibility equation, and the line equalizer supplies exactly one without changing carrier support.

physicalReopeningDatum.required: Source the common coefficient line as a physical spurion, correspondence-module map, boundary datum or universal matching object, and compute its embeddings into the actual selected Dirac and Majorana Pati-Salam Hom lines.
tests: the embeddings and their J partners are nonzero and normalized
the family-anchor action realizes them without a Gamma_rel-odd carrier edge
the spectator connector and physical junk quotient do not create an independent mixed I-N primitive
loops preserve the one-dimensional coefficient equalizer
physicalReopeningDatum.falsifier: two independent source coefficient lines or a required Gamma_rel-odd carrier sewing

verdict: The smallest viable sewing is not an operator between the two relation carriers. It is a one-dimensional common-source equalizer of their coefficient lines. This formally derives the common Schur ray while retaining typed noncomposability, but its physical source is still missing.
